name: walmsley2024_spray_dryer
description: Milk powder spray dryer (main air chamber, static and vibrating fluid beds, exhaust air with heat recovery). Loads in kW. Table 1 data as published.
reference: Walmsley, Lincoln, Padullés, Cleland (2024), Energies 17, 2838, Table 1 (case first presented by Liang et al.).

provenance.stream data: published (Table 1). WARNING: Table 1 is inconsistent with the paper's own targets (4.98 / 3.99 MW) by the first law; see verify_walmsley2024.py
provenance.source_T_C: assumed: 15 °C (dead state), where the cooled exhaust air ends
provenance.sink levels: assumed, illustrative: 120 °C (fluid beds) and 200 °C (upper end of IEA HPT Annex 58 scope); the main air chamber up to 236 °C stays on fired heating
provenance.basis: published: 6000 h/year, Liang et al. (2022), 'Full electrification opportunities of spray dryers in milk powder processes', ECOS 2022, Copenhagen (DTU accepted manuscript, peer-reviewed): the source of the stream data in Walmsley et al. (2024) Table 1 (GEA Process Engineering, skim milk powder dryer), Sec. 2.1
provenance.economics: assumed: no economic data in the source (see economics.sources)
provenance.film coefficients: Liang et al. (2022), Table 2 (from Zühlsdorf et al.): overall U water-air 42.5 W/(m2 K) on the air-side area. Air-air heat transfer is done through water loops (direct air-air exchange is not used in practice, Sec. 2.1), i.e. two water-air exchangers in series: h = 0.0425 kW/(m2 K) per air stream gives U = 21 W/(m2 K) per match
provenance.eta_lorenz_sensitivity: 0.45-0.52: Lorenz (Carnot) efficiencies implied by the DEA catalogue HTHP sheets 2.a/2.b (COP 4.45/2.75/2.4/2.05 at lifts of 40/65/80/100 K), as for the brewery
provenance.COP check: HTHP 120 °C (105 K lift): COP 1.87 vs DEA sheet 2.a about 1.96 at 105 K (-4.6 %, conservative). HTHP 200 °C: COP 1.28 from a 15 °C source; Liang et al. (2022) use the exhaust (via water loops) as source and reach COP 2.61 for the steam heat pump, Liang et al. (2023, IIR ICR) a total COP of 2.68 with a transcritical CO2 cycle: the illustrative isothermal design here is pessimistic

economics._note: No economic data in the source. Prices: Eurostat Portugal 2026-S1 for the site's consumption band at 8000 h/year; heat pump investment: Danish Energy Agency catalogue by sink temperature with its lift and steam add-ons; other parameters: tool defaults (Sources page). All are assumptions for this case.

dea_lift_2a.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.a: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.15 M€/MW (0.05-0.25)

dea_lift_2b.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheet 2.b: 'Additional equipment cost for temperature lift above 75 K' 0.2 M€/MW (0.1-0.3)

dea_steam.source: Danish Energy Agency, Technology Data - Industrial Process Heat (2025), 2025 values, sheets 2.a and 2.b: 'Steam generation increases equipment cost by' 0.2 M€/MW (0.05-0.3); applied to isothermal sinks (steam). The sheets' COP penalty for steam (-0.15) is not applied: COP comes from the Lorenz model

sources.prices: Eurostat nrg_pc_203 (gas) and nrg_pc_205 (electricity), Portugal, 2026-S1, excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes and levies, EUR/kWh, gas on GCV (data/sources/eurostat_portugal_prices.csv). The plant is not in Portugal: these prices place it in the dissertation's context. Bands at the published 6000 h/year: powder rate not published (air flows only: main air 77,762 kg/h, Liang et al. 2022 Table 1); estimated 8.3 t/h from the air heating (6.03 MW) and 2,610 MJ/t air-heater use (Walmsley et al. 2016, CET 52). Gas 5.2 GJ/t x 8.3 x 6000 = 0.26 million GJ (I4, 0.0445); electricity 220 kWh/t x 8.3 x 6000 = 11 GWh + heat pumps 14.7 GWh = 26 GWh (IE, 0.0897). Both bands hold for any plant between 4 and 32 t/h, so the estimate does not change the prices
sources.heat_pump_cost: Danish Energy Agency catalogue (2025) by sink temperature, linear in capacity, plus the catalogue's add-ons for lift above 75 K (sink outlet minus source outlet) and steam generation (isothermal sinks). Replaces Padullés et al. (2026, Table 3), which is fitted to brewery heat pumps and gives 0.75-0.88 M€/MW for 2-3 MW units, below the catalogue range 0.9-1.5 M€/MW for sinks up to 125 °C. Indirect cost of new hot-water piping (0.23 M€/MW, 'relevant when needing to install new hot water piping instead of existing steam piping') is a scenario, not in the base. Steam add-on only for the 200 °C level: in Liang et al. (2022), 'Full electrification opportunities of spray dryers in milk powder processes', ECOS 2022, Copenhagen (DTU accepted manuscript, peer-reviewed): the source of the stream data in Walmsley et al. (2024) Table 1 (GEA Process Engineering, skim milk powder dryer) the existing dryer heats air with steam heaters from a steam boiler (Fig. 1, Sec. 2.4); in the electrified design the NH3 and hydrocarbon heat pumps deliver hot-water loops (water loops avoid product contamination, Sec. 2.1) and only the top unit is a closed-loop steam heat pump
sources.comparison: Liang et al. (2022), 5 %/20 y, 6000 h, renewable electricity 40 €/MWh, Danish gas 31 €/MWh incl. taxes, boiler 0.9: full electrification (NH3 + hydrocarbon + steam heat pumps, water loops, > 12,000 m2 of air-water exchangers) TCI 8.1-8.4 M€, levelised cost of heat 35.1-36.2 €/MWh vs 35.8 for the gas boiler; steam heat pump COP 2.61 (Lorenz efficiency 33 %), other heat pumps COP > 2

area_targeting.film_coefficients_source: Liang et al. (2022), Table 2 (from Zühlsdorf et al.): overall U water-air 42.5 W/(m2 K) on the air-side area. Air-air heat transfer is done through water loops (direct air-air exchange is not used in practice, Sec. 2.1), i.e. two water-air exchangers in series: h = 0.0425 kW/(m2 K) per air stream gives U = 21 W/(m2 K) per match
area_targeting._cost: no verified cost law: Liang et al. (2022) Table 3 fit installed fin-and-tube costs, log10(C) = 5.8265 - 1.0102 log10(A) + 0.2192 log10(A)^2 (A air-side, 10-6500 m2, 1998 basis from their ref. [28]), i.e. about 480, 60 and 22 per m2 at 100, 1000 and 6500 m2; it cannot be escalated here (currency and CEPCI 1998 not verified), so it only sets the order of the sweep
area_targeting._cold_utility: the exhaust is vented to atmosphere: no cooling utility cost

retrofit_bounds.note: Liang et al. (2022), Sec. 2.1 and Fig. 1: in the standard installation the inlet air is not heated by the exhaust (no air-to-air exchange), every air stream is heated by steam heaters and the exhaust is vented. Their electrified design recovers exhaust heat through water loops, which the film coefficients here represent (two water-air exchangers per match). The new-network cost uses the sweep (no verified air-water exchanger cost law)
retrofit_bounds.hen_cost_note: not a cost estimate: Liang et al. (2022) Table 3 fin-and-tube fit gives about 72 per m2 at 756 m2 per unit on a 1998 basis (currency and escalation not verified); costs have risen since. 100 €/m2 also gives dTmin,opt 8 K in step 3, the approach of Liang's minimum cost of heat
